correctness.rationale: The fixed point has zero in every even global position, hence all ones of any factor occupy one relative parity; it also avoids 11 and 0000. For every length m, the morphism induces a bijection between qualifying conjugacy classes of length m and 2m: an aligned representative uniquely desubstitutes, every conjugate desubstitutes from an even-aligned occurrence, and conversely even and odd rotations of a morphic image are realized from occurrences of conjugates. Odd shifts cannot collapse two distinct classes except for the all-zero image, which is excluded for m>=2. At odd length at least five, a qualifying circular word must contain at least two ones, and a cut separating two ones produces a rotation with ones of both parities, impossible in the fixed point. The base cases n=1 and n=3 each have exactly two classes. The verifier independently enumerates all factors and Lie classes through length 192.

value.rationale: Bell and Shallit introduced Lie complexity specifically to quantify factors whose entire cyclic conjugacy class remains in a language and devoted a section to exact formulas for classical automatic words. The period-doubling word is a canonical 2-automatic fixed point omitted from those examples. The result gives not only the automatic output sequence but a complete structural classification of the two surviving classes at every nonzero length, with an exact morphic doubling law and an obstruction eliminating all other odd parts.
